The own page shows 4.10 MB while the article reports 108 MB; compression or version change was not verified. No TIFF was downloaded. DataCite API returned 404 for this older DOI.
description: Researchers at the Chinese Academy of Sciences linked 2010 population counts to township and subdistrict boundaries across 31 provincial-level areas of China. The public Science Data Bank version-one record describes 42,122 matched spatial units, boundary-topology corrections and conversion to a TIFF density layer. The describing China Scientific Data article gives a 1-kilometre grid and a 2010 snapshot. The own page states CC BY 4.0. Healthcare, emergency-service and other infrastructure simulations can use the surface to locate potential users or people exposed to hazards. Township averages cannot represent household locations or population movement within a township, and the layer does not describe current demand after 2010. The team reports provincial deviations below ten percent and overall accuracy of 99 percent, but that aggregate comparison is not a cell-level uncertainty map. The own page lists a much smaller file size than the article, so this draft does not assert a payload size. The TIFF was not downloaded or checked. Related WorldPop catalogue records provide different gridded population estimates that may be compared before choosing an exposure baseline.
